NO ONE is safe when Trump’s federal agents and attorneys lie to the courts.

The law only protects us when the government tells the truth.

Federal Judge Sara Ellis’ 233 page opinion found federal agents lied so frequently in their reports and testimony about Operation Midway Blitz that it was hard to believe anything they said was truthful. ICE agents' claims directly contradicted their own body camera footage.

Just a few examples:

• September 26, Broadview: In his report, an agent claimed protestors were “becoming increasingly hostile.” The video proves they were just standing peacefully before agents attacked with tear gas, pepper balls and clubs.

• October 4, Brighton Park: Agents claimed their use of force was justified by stating protestors threw things – completely reversing the sequence of events.

• October 12, Albany Park: DHS publicly claimed a bicyclist threw a bike at agents. The video makes clear the opposite happened: agents threw tear gas first, then it was actually the AGENTS took a protestor’s bike and threw it, knocking protestors to the ground.

One agent even used ChatGPT to fabricate his use-of-force report.

We deserve leaders who will stand up to say: this systematic abuse of power is not acceptable in our country.

Most AI corporations are fighting to remain completely unregulated, with no safeguards against the potential existential risks AI poses to our planet, our economy, and our democracy.

That’s why I’ll fight for a national data center NDA ban, moratoriums on building data centers to let local and state governments assess the real costs without being rolled by mega-corporations bullying them, and serious environmental protections that safeguard our neighborhoods and peaceful communities.

And for the AI images and content these data centers produce? I’ll require companies to build guardrails, and I’ll fight to create public-interest safety oversight agencies for these groups and to establish legal causes of action to hold corporations accountable.

The US needs to lead the way in creating binding international agreements that establish a global AI safety regime as we do with many other dangerous technologies, such as those used for biological, chemical, and nuclear weapons and energy technology.

Deepfake videos are often deceptive attempts to mislead constituents, undermine elections, cheat consumers, and harass children and adults with nonconsensual sexual content churned out by these AI companies with little to no recourse. The concerns about AI taking jobs are real, too, and we have to find ways to balance the real-world use of AI with the outright harm it causes to working families and individuals.

Left on their own, they have proven inconsistent in self-regulation at best, disastrously reckless at worst. A consistent, public-first set of guardrails is a vital prerequisite for making AI safe enough to actually serve the public good rather than only AI’s billionaire (or trillionaire!) shareholders.
without the world’s biggest corporations threatening them and forcing them into secretive NDAs.

Campaigns used to pay thousands of dollars and wait weeks to get a logo for their campaigns. Now, with the use of AI, they can do it for free. Look at what AI was able to put together for us in a matter of seconds!  By stealing other people's work, AI will finally democratize democracy!

7 in 10 Americans oppose data centers in their area, but Kaela Berg and Matt Klein voted to give the richest corporations in the world massive tax breaks to build data centers in Minnesota. 

Under that bill, companies like Meta, OpenAI, and Google will receive a tax break for 35 YEARS (!!!), worth at least $300 million in the first two years and potentially tens of billions over the coming decades, just by building their data centers here in Minnesota. 

Entire communities feel blindsided by the impact these massive centers have on their way of life. Noise, light, air, and water pollution concerns go unheard because local leaders are signing NDA’s, and serve at the behest of these companies, not their fellow citizens.

I’ve been a city councilor and a mayor. I know what it feels like to fight for your town, to fight for jobs and housing. But that stability can’t come at the cost of long-term health and millions of taxpayer dollars in secret meetings.

When I’m elected to Congress, I’ll fight to regulate these data centers, ban the signing of NDAs by elected officials, and I won’t give one more cent of taxpayer money to these companies.

We wanted to hear about what issues concerned young voters, and you spoke loud and clear. You’re worried about AI, reckless data centers that are polluting our water and hiking energy prices, and healthcare. Me too! 

We can only fix these problems if we fight. I grew up experiencing many of the same worries you have. My dad lost his job during the tech bubble's burst in the late '90s, and my mom has been sick all my life. 

We need generational change and progressive leadership if we’re going to make it happen. And I’m going to fight tooth and nail to make it happen. If you believe in regulating AI and big tech, if you believe in Medicare for All and an end to money in politics, I need you to do a few things for me:

We’ve got three days left before August 11th– vote early, or vote on August 11th for Matt Little

Get your friends and family to vote

And join our fight– we’ve got door knocks tomorrow that could use your help! 
If you believe a better world is possible, you’ve got a place with us!
We've been pushing for a moratorium. Policies and regulations and actual studies and factual information, we need to gather all that up before we start plopping these things everywhere.

It’s a local, state and federal issue, but I view the federal government's role as always providing a minimum standard of rights. [...] So, just trying to protect people in the short term by using a moratorium until we can get these regulations updated.

When the tech bubble burst in the late ‘90s, my Dad was suddenly out of a job and out of luck. 

His old associate's degree was obsolete, and he no longer had a place in the economy. 

The same thing is happening now to millions of workers across the country with the sudden adoption of AI. Entry-level jobs have started to disappear. 

Degrees we told students to pursue even four years ago have, in some cases, completely lost their relevance. 

We need strong leaders and a plan to ensure workers displaced by AI can still find their place in this economy, support their families, and eventually retire. 

When I get to Washington, I’ll regulate data centers and the AI work they produce, and ensure that we hold these ultra-wealthy companies accountable.

Elon Musk’s Grok AI is being used to create explicit images of minors.   Now, he’s suing Minnesota for daring to pass a law that bans nudification by AI. 

I sat down with the authors of the AI Nudification Ban bill, State Senator Erin Maye Quade, State Representative Jess Hanson, and U.S. Congressman Greg Casar (TX-35) to discuss the bill and what we can do to rein in AI.   Elon Musk and Grok AI are enabling criminals. They are allowing millions of people, children and adults alike, to be violated by malicious actors.

When we get to Washington and take back the house, we’re going to regulate these companies and ensure that these machines can’t be used to violate you or your children.   Thank you to Senator Maye Quade and Representative Hanson for leading this fight, and to Congressman Casar for taking the time to be with us today!

In 2025, Eric Pratt voted for H.F. 16, which gave data centers over $300 MILLION in tax breaks. But that’s not all. 

Those tax breaks? 

They last 35 YEARS.   That means BILLIONS in your tax dollars will fill the pockets of Elon Musk and other tech billionaires.   They can claim software, construction materials, and even the energy they use to receive these tax breaks.   Now, Eric Pratt is OPPOSING data center moratoriums, leaving local communities to fight against billion dollar companies–alone. The federal government and our representatives can’t skirt their responsibility.   As elected leaders, you should listen to your constituents. CD2 has been loud and clear–NO MORE SECRET NDA’S. These shady practices have prevented constituents from hearing all the pros and cons of these data centers.   A moratorium puts power back in the hands of local communities. It ensures that families and neighborhoods receive all the information they need to make an informed decision about data centers, until we can regulate AI right.  

When I get to Washington, I won’t give another cent to tech billionaires. I’ll fight for our local communities, ban secretive NDA’s, and pass strict environmental regulations that protect your energy bill and your drinking water.

Lindsay Isaacs, a 23-year-old Floridian, spent 13 days in jail, two weeks on bond, and had her car confiscated by police for 10 months after being misidentified by Flock cameras and their AI software. In an interview conducted by News Nation, Isaacs stated, “It was a nightmare I was living.”

Investigators searched for the first Dodge Durango they found on Flock cameras in the area and pinned the crime on Isaacs. There are no safeguards or statutes regulating Flock, and no steps were taken to prevent something like this in the future. 

Isaacs and her lawyer are arguing, “Defendants fabricated evidence of vehicle damage, swore to false statements in an affidavit for an arrest warrant, and at a bond/pretrial detention hearing, and ignored readily available exculpatory evidence.” 

The CEO of Flock refused to comment about this specific instance, but he continued to push that we, as a country, need to pick safety and surveillance over privacy. Their ability to make up entire stories and evidence using AI poses new and frightening prospects for our justice system. People’s lives could be at risk due to Flock cameras and the ability to fabricate evidence and pin it on an individual.

Washington can’t sit back– we must ban Flock cameras, and restore Americans' right to privacy. When I get to Washington, that’s exactly what I’ll do.

We have AI companies and former researchers coming out and saying clearly what many of us have known all along: 

AI needs to be regulated.

I don’t find our current position with AI exciting, unlike my opponent, Eric Pratt. I’m concerned. I’m concerned that children are getting access to chatbots that coax them into self harm. 

I’m concerned that our artists and creatives are experiencing the largest theft of their work in human history. 

I’m concerned that every day workers are going to lose their jobs, and that we have no safety nets to ensure they can support their families.  

We need to regulate AI, and we need to do it now. We need a one year moratorium on data centers so local communities can learn all the environmental and energy concerns, and put their own zoning and regulatory laws in place. 

I’m not excited by a future where this technology is left to run amok. That’s why when I get to Washington, we’ll put these regulations in place and protect our communities and working families.

When I get to Washington, we’re going to ensure that these AI and tech companies meet the highest safety standards.
